scope: Bind the accepted reserve-readiness interface to actual autonomous settlement and actual paid-work interruption. Completion kind and grade come only from the realized native traversal; callers cannot assert success, support, grade, route or reserve effect. This closes the FT5.2 integration gate while retaining FT5.3 depletion, recovery, full grid comparison and release-policy election.
rules: One controller owns one IntegratedDemandController and one ReserveCandidateController paired to the same native engine, actor and exact ReserveLedger. It accepts only historical state, one exact Demand and a positive work bound; the native request and route remain autonomously formed and selected.

The reserve demand is admitted only through FT5.2b1 after the owned request exists. Any positive preparation remains a visible separate phase. Only FT5.2a-bound paid post-admission jobs can make it ready, after which the unchanged FT4 route policy re-evaluates and launches native work.

Completion is possible only after the actual selected traversal succeeds, its exact movement output is consumed by paid same-scope native work, and the FT4 demand controller commits settlement. No selection label, partial job, deferred route, failed consumer or evaluator input can complete reserve accounting.

A realized traversal whose supported field is true and whose selected means is support records supported completion. Every other settled traversal records independent completion. The controller accepts no completion-kind or support flag.

For grade-load-v1 independent completion, last_paid_grade is derived from hle_unified.model_g.grade of the actual traversal target seat. Null and load-v1 receive no grade input. Supported completion never receives a grade input.

An interruption is allowed only while the autonomous request remains unsettled and after authoritative native route work for that request has spent a positive amount. Preparation work alone is not route work. The controller derives one immutable attempt identity and exact paid-job evidence; interruption loses at most one reserve unit and leaves the owned demand pending.

Terminal steps and one recorded interruption are idempotent at the integration boundary. FT5.1 continues to reject replayed attempt identities. A completion or interruption reserve event is appended exactly once and cannot refund, mint or reprice the native wallet.

Zero reserve remains bounded at zero and never removes a demand, capability or any of the six FT4 route options. Preparation units, native energy/time, reserve balance and completion/interruption delta remain separate exact fields.

The checkpoint commits the paired native hash, exact demand-controller state, exact candidate/binding/ledger state, autonomous request and phase, consumer identity, terminal event and integration events. Restore rejects different native state or inconsistent event order and continues exactly.

The independent auditor imports no reserve-cycle controller. It audits the embedded candidate and native ledgers, reconstructs autonomous request ownership, paid traversal/consumer/settlement links, actual support and grade, authoritative paid interruption evidence, exact reserve deltas and one-use identities.

Acceptance requires the fifteen exact new methods, all one hundred seventy-one FT5.2b1/FT5.2a/FT5.1/FT4 predecessor identities, canonical and workflow witnesses, registered fixtures, a strict source freeze and unchanged source.

Passing closes only FT5.2 candidate-dynamics integration. FT5.3 still owes sustained depletion, restart, external replenishment, harder-demand partial order, the preregistered grid and release-policy selection. C13/TD4 realism and psychology remain unvalidated.
gate: Fifteen exact FT5.2b2 methods pass with zero failures/errors; independent and supported completion plus actual paid interruption have reconstructible exact effects under all three policies; no partial, deferred, preparation-only or caller-asserted event changes reserve; native prices and all six routes remain unchanged; all 171 predecessor identities remain exact.
next: FT5.3 sustained depletion, recovery, harder-demand order, frozen grid and release-policy decision
stop: Preserve failures; two gate failures after correction stops.
